text:
alex: heads-up — customer reported autorouter picked apply_credit instead of refund for a partial refund. request_id r-9f3aa. hitting hosted API v1.
morgan: can you paste the original payload and any error snippets?
alex: here it is:
```json
{
  "customer_id": "cus_123",
  "intent": "refund",
  "amount": 1250,
  "currency": "usd",
  "reason": "partial refund for duplicate charge",
  "metadata": {"line_item": "order_987"}
}
```
morgan: quick hypothesis: resolver matched aliases. apply_credit signature overlaps with refund (both accept amount/currency), and apply_credit has fewer required fields so it squeaked ahead.
gina: looking at the trace: router resolved apply_credit (score=0.82) vs refund (score=0.79) — close call. deploy-bot emitted resolver scores in the trace.
alex: customer saw no refund; they got an internal note. logs show apply_credit failed validation then fallback created support note.
morgan: paste logs:
```
[2026-03-15T12:04:21Z] router: resolved apply_credit (score=0.82) vs refund (score=0.79)
[2026-03-15T12:04:21Z] executor: invoking apply_credit with args {"customer_id":"cus_123","amount":1250,"currency":"usd"}
[2026-03-15T12:04:21Z] executor:error validationFailed field=credit_source required
[2026-03-15T12:04:21Z] fallback: created support_note id:n-555
```
gina: repro steps are straightforward — hit /v1/actions with that payload and resolver picks apply_credit every time for this customer. It's deterministic because customer profile lacks credit_source (they have allow_credits=false) which means apply_credit will fail schema validation downstream.

morgan: root cause: tie-break uses static heuristic (schema length + alias score). apply_credit had slightly higher combined score. No runtime check for "will this tool actually validate given derived context".

alex: suggested mitigations:
- tighten alias fuzzy matching for refund vs credit synonyms (reduce accidental collisions)
- add derived-context compatibility scoring: if context indicates no credit allowed, penalize apply_credit heavily
- on validation failure, if second-best tool within threshold (0.05) then retry resolver with next candidate
- short-term: adjust apply_credit base weight by -0.1 in prod for the next 24h (hotfix) while we patch matcher

gina: support action: manual refund done for cus_123, filed reimbursement ticket. leaving note to customer.
support-bot: created internal ticket SUP-9274: "resolver misrouted to apply_credit causing failed refund; hotfix + resolver patch". assigned to morgan. :white_check_mark:

eng-sre: added a metric to alert on increased fallback notes and validation-failures-per-resolver. Will watch for spikes during canary.
morgan: I'll own the resolver rule change. plan: start with compatibility scoring + conservative alias thresholds. Canary to 10% of router traffic.
alex: ok thanks — pls post canary results and we can consider weight hotfix if needed. :thumbsup:

gina: one more detail — payload had metadata.line_item which previously biased the router toward apply_credit in a few past incidents (legacy synonym mapping). I'll remove that legacy alias.
alex: great. keep me posted.
support-bot: note SUP-9274 updated: milestone=canary-deploy scheduled 2026-03-16.
alex: ack."
